title: Derivative of a translated interval average
statement: Let $\eta>0$ and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. For every $x\in\mathbb R$, the translated interval average $S_\eta\psi$ is differentiable at $x$, with derivative $\bigl(\psi(x+\eta)-\psi(x)\bigr)/\eta$.
replaced: For $\eta>0$ and a real function $\psi$, write $S_\eta\psi(x)=\eta^{-1}\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt$. If $\psi$ is continuous, then $S_\eta\psi$ is differentiable at every real $x$ with derivative $(\psi(x+\eta)-\psi(x))/\eta$.
